# 1 Enoch Chapter 56 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS | **Section:** Book of Parables

---

**56:1** And-I-saw there the-hosts of-the-angels of-punishment going, and-they were-holding rods of-iron and-bronze.

**56:2** And-I-asked the-angel of-peace who-went with-me, saying: To-whom are-these going who-are-holding [those] rods? And-he-said unto-me: To-their-elect and-beloved-ones, that-they-may-be-cast into the-chasm of the-judgment of that-valley.

**56:3** And-then-that valley shall-be-filled with-their-elect and-beloved, and-the-days of-their-lives shall-be-at-an-end, and-the-days of-their-leading-astray shall-henceforth not-be-reckoned.

**56:4** And-in-those-days the-angels shall-return and-shall-assemble toward the-east, toward the-Parthians and-the-Medes: they-shall-stir-up the-kings, so-that a-spirit of-unrest shall-come-upon-them, and-they-shall-drive-them from-their-thrones, [so-that] they-shall-break-out like-lions from-their-dens, and-as-hungry-wolves among their-flocks.

**56:5** And-they-shall-go-up and-tread-under-foot the-land of-His-elect-ones, and-the-land of-His-elect shall-be before them a-threshing-floor and-a-highway.

**56:6** But-the-city of-my-righteous shall-be a-hindrance to-their-horses. And-they-shall-begin-to-fight-among-themselves, and-their-right-hand shall-be-strong against-themselves, and-a-man shall-not-know his-brother, nor-a-son his-father or-his-mother, till-there-be no-number of-the-corpses through-their-slaughter, and-their-punishment-be not-in-vain.

**56:7** And-in-those-days Sheol shall-open its-jaws, and-they-shall-be-swallowed-up therein: and-their-destruction shall-be-at-an-end. Sheol shall-devour the-sinners in-the-presence of-the-elect.

**56:8** And-it-came-to-pass after this that-I-saw another host of-wagons of-men, and-the-women riding upon-them, and-they came from-the-west unto-the-east.

---

*EMET notes: Translated from the Ge'ez (Ethiopic) text. Hyphenated compounds preserve Ge'ez construct chains. Ch. 56 describes the angelic armies going against the Parthians and Medes, followed by eschatological warfare in which Sheol swallows the sinners. 'Elect-ones' throughout preserves the Ge'ez heruyan.*
